cells.tense: Right now, with nothing behind the ledger.
cells.verb: giving and taking with people in even measure
cells.place: in the place where you become fully yourself
cells.ask: If you want it: pick one thing a recent trade with someone left you holding — a skill, a habit, a way of seeing — and let the older version of yourself it replaced finish ending. Keep the new thing in a shape that lasts. Then the giving and the receiving keep flowing without you having to watch them.
cells.core: What you hand people and what they hand you are coming out about even, and that evenness is part of how you're becoming who you are. You're not shrinking to fit what someone gave you, and you're not swelling to cover what you owe — you take what's offered, offer what's yours, and both arrive in the open. Who you are gets built partly in that back-and-forth, and it shows.
cells.sheetLine: You're becoming yourself in fair trade with the people around you.

cells.tense: You're already in the moment where the account comes due.
cells.verb: keeping every trade with people squared to the penny
cells.place: in the place where you become fully yourself
cells.ask: Try this: let one thing stay owed — by you or to you — for a week, and carry it without moving to settle it. Notice that you still stand, that the weight sits in you without crushing anything. What comes back is a sense of what's fair that doesn't need the math, and giving and receiving that flow instead of being counted.
cells.core: Every time someone gives you something, you're already working out what you'll give back, and whether it'll be enough. Somewhere ahead is a version of you who has repaid everyone and been repaid in full, and you're living toward that person — so who you actually are keeps getting rewritten to fit the tally. You can't become yourself while auditing the exchange that's forming you.
cells.sheetLine: You're settling the score so fast nobody gets to just give you anything.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.verb: letting what you give and take with people run thin
cells.place: in the place where you become fully yourself
cells.ask: Don't force yourself back into the trading yet. Instead, sit alone for an hour with one thing you've been building on your own and sort it — exactly which part of it is yours to offer, and exactly which part you'd be glad to receive from someone. The sorting does the pulling. Once you can tell the two apart, giving and receiving start to move on their own.
cells.core: You've been becoming who you are mostly by yourself. Somewhere back there, trading openly with people stopped feeling worth it, and you kept the door shut after the reason was gone. What's missing isn't the self — that's still forming. It's that nobody gets to add to it, and you don't get to add to anyone.
cells.sheetLine: You're becoming yourself with the door shut, and the door is behind you.

cells.tense: Pen down, in a room you've been writing the whole time.
cells.verb: receiving from people and giving back in fair measure
cells.place: in the place where you become fully yourself
cells.ask: Before you call the next good thing in yourself self-made, hold one question for a day without answering it out loud: who handed me part of this? Let the knowing arrive on its own; you don't have to announce it. What returns is receiving in the open, with your name on the taking as well as the giving.
cells.core: Who you're becoming is being shaped by what people hand you and what you hand back — it's running every day, and others can see it. But you'd describe the result as something you made alone. The trading is already happening. The part where you say so, where you let yourself be someone who was given to, hasn't.
cells.sheetLine: You're already being given to. You just call it self-made.
